brief: Goldman strategist Natasha Tiwana's weekly 'Global Reflections', relayed here by Zero Hedge, argues equities are capped and floored at the same time. Elevated risk appetite and growth-shock risk limit upside, while the de-rating already done and room to scale back hawkish rates pricing cut the odds of a large drawdown, so September's FOMC tips it either way. Waller leaned on hold, which scaled back September hike pricing, then payrolls pushed that pricing back up. Because AI's weight blunts vanilla index hedges, SPXXAI is the preferred broad hedge and the implied vol reset has kept tactical hedging demand up. Contained index vol sits over high thematic and factor vol, with momentum down 5% year-to-date. Yield volatility drives rate-sensitive basket demand, and non-profitable tech is reverting after a year pricing lower rates that never came. Into midterms equities historically go sideways, so the note works baskets: ACA-exposed names benefit and drug makers suffer if Democrats take a chamber, non-defense spending could rise, and power infrastructure is a buy as the datacenter fight shifts to who pays for power. French domestics are rich and exposed to wider OAT-Bund spreads. Watch European gas, not oil: Dec26 TTF could reach 100 EUR/MWh versus 71 now.
